blueprint_concepts: Evaluation of limit involving exponential and logarithmic functions
solution_full: For $0<|x|<1$ both powers are defined: $(1+x)^{2x}=e^{2x\log_{e}(1+x)}$ and $(1-x)^{-2x}=e^{-2x\log_{e}(1-x)}$.
Their difference is $-2x^{3}+O(x^{4})$, and the limit is $-2$.
originality_note: New: two mirror-image variable powers whose second-order terms are equal and whose third-order terms are opposite, so the difference is of order x^3 (way 4, hidden symmetry). Closest known: lim ((1+x)^(1/x) - e)/x. Different because: the exponents grow with x (not 1/x), and the cancellation of the x^2 terms is the point.

concept_use.Exponential and logarithmic series (e^x,: The logarithmic series of log(1+x), log(1-x) and the exponential series e^u = 1 + u + O(u^2) give the expansions.
concept_use.Evaluation of limit involving exponentia: The limit of a quotient of exponential-logarithmic expressions is read from the x^3 coefficient.

stem_review: Read as a student: the limit is a single expression defined for 0 < |x| < 1; answer -2 is a negative integer as planned (sympy limit checked); Hindi mirrors. No change.
key_step: Write both powers as e^(x log) and expand to order x^3.
justification: Composition of the logarithmic and exponential series with order bookkeeping; two linked series ideas, numerical. Above 2024-P2-Q3 (L1, 1^infinity limit) and below 2025-P1-Q11 (L4).
